items.title: Live: Trump says US 'no longer' needs NATO allies, Australia in Iran war
items.description: Donald Trump says the US "do not need the help of anyone" in the war against Iran, calling out NATO allies and Australia in a fiery social media post. Follow live.

items.title: What Ali Larijani's death will mean for Iran, plus what else you should know
items.description: The ABC's Middle East correspondent Matthew Doran is in Beirut and is providing daily updates on the Middle East war.

items.title: Trump names Australia in outburst over lack of ally support in Iran
items.description: The United States president has declared America does "not need the help of anyone" in the war he launched against Iran, days after he called on allies to help reclaim a key shipping route.

items.title: Live: Andrew Hastie labels Trump's outburst at allies, Australia 'petulant'
items.description: Liberal frontbencher Andrew Hastie has labelled the US president's outburst at allies as "petulant" and says that the rules-based order is "dead". Follow live.

items.title: Australia-bound medicines rerouted as Middle East war escalates
items.description: The Middle East war is forcing major pharmaceutical companies to divert critical medicines away from one of the world's most important trade routes, to ensure there are no supply issues in Australia.

items.title: RBA governor warns of the recession we might have to have
items.description: Is the RBA fighting last year's inflation war with its latest interest rate hike? Whatever the case may be, Australians are bracing for even more economic pain.

items.title: Three states in firing line of rare triple-hit cyclone
items.description: The last Australian triple landfall system was Severe Tropical Cyclone Ingrid more than two decades ago.

items.title: 'Over to my lawyers': Kyle Sandilands sacked by ARN Media
items.description: Kyle Sandilands has announced he has been sacked by ARN Media after an on-air row with co-host Jackie Henderson last month.

items.title: To fix the generation gap, Labor may have to leave the grandfathers behind
items.description: A Senate committee report into the capital gains tax was authored by the Greens but littered with clues about Labor's plans.

items.title: Surge in 'increasingly real' fake cash arriving in Australia
items.description: Cash may have declined in use during COVID but the use of it has steadied since. But technology has also opened a door to fake cash and its being seized now at much higher levels.

items.title: IVF industry again under scrutiny after 'epic error' revealed by DNA test
items.description: Fertility experts say the discovery of an IVF mix-up at Royal North Shore Hospital in 1995 could be the tip of the iceberg as more Australians research their parentage.

items.title: Quick hits: Sam Kerr provides geometric genius as Katrina Gorry takes a battering
items.description: Sam Kerr gets her angles right, Katrina Gorry stands tall despite a battering and Kaitlyn Torpey has a birthday to remember. Here are the quick hits from the Matildas' exhilirating 2-1 semifinal triumph over China.

items.title: Court transcription service in crisis after entering voluntary administration
items.description: Four weeks after the ABC revealed sensitive court files were being accessed offshore in a potential risk to national security, the company responsible for the breach has entered into voluntary administration.

items.title: Bali becomes a ghost town for new year. Here's why
items.description: Instead of fireworks and countdowns, Bali rings in its new year in complete silence.

items.title: A hidden world keeps one of Australia's oldest museums running
items.description: Museums display only a fraction of their collection so we went behind the scenes at the Melbourne Museum to find the untold stories kept from public view.

items.title: 'You have to laugh': Why this critique of corporate work culture is a comedy
items.description: This dark comedy takes aim at capitalism and corporate work culture, but it also finds hope in the relationships between everyday people.

items.title: Quiz: Do you have the frequent flyers points to pass our test?
items.description: Which country’s currency is called the quetzal? And what is Thailand's Songkran festival best known for?

items.title: Chronic conditions dismissed as anxiety, low iron
items.description: Young women have detailed their experiences being dismissed and misdiagnosed as chronic pain sufferers. Now, they're teaching others how to advocate for their health.

items.title: One Nation is tipped to be a major player in the SA election
items.description: One Nation South Australia candidate Rocco DeAngelis says people are "disappointed" in the major parties ahead of the state election, but Greens SA leader Robert Simms says the party is "scapegoating minority groups".

items.title: Live: Chance of RBA interest rate hike in May drops to 40pc, ASX opens slightly higher
items.description: The Australian share market has begun its day slightly higher, while the likelihood of a follow-up interest rate hike in May has fallen substantially after the Reserve Bank's 5-4 vote in favour of yesterday's rate increase — the slimmest of majorities. Follow live.

items.title: Higher oil costs set to spike prices well beyond the fuel pump
items.description: From mining to agriculture, higher oil prices from the war in the Middle East are not only increasing fuel costs, but prices for key chemicals as well. Can businesses cope?

items.title: New CCTV footage as police hunt more kidnappers over grandfather's murder
items.description: Police have released new video showing three men they believe were involved in the mistaken identity kidnapping and murder of Sydney grandfather Chris Baghsarian last month.

items.title: Report finds 'significant and sustained shift' in support for salmon industry
items.description: A CSIRO report has found Tasmania's salmon farming industry has experienced a "significant and sustained shift" away from strong community support it experienced a decade ago.

items.title: Density push to allow for 20-storey towers in Melbourne's north
items.description: The Victorian government has released its final planning controls for 25 activity centres in Melbourne, with tweaks meaning lower height limits in parts of Kew and Oakleigh and higher heights in parts of Coburg and Brunswick.

items.title: Fuel and fertiliser shortage hits at crunch time for farmers
items.description: Farmers are warning consumers to expect price rises in the supermarket as fuel and fertiliser shortages affect crop production and transport.
